children: Deep Yellow's bull at Jefferies cuts its price target by 37% to A$1.20/share after the aspiring uranium miner delays a final investment decision on its Tumas project. Deep Yellow decided to wait because equity and credit markets are too weak right now. Analyst Daniel Roden now assumes Deep Yellow proceeds with Tumas in June 2027, with first ore produced in October 2029. "Deferral preserves financing flexibility, although schedule slippage, capital escalation and higher operating costs erode net present value," Jefferies says. "We expect updated project metrics, funding and FID within 12 months, subject to market conditions." Deep Yellow ended last week at A$0.82. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
